user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
It depends on the reason code, because each one has a different window counted from the transaction date (2026-07-20). Based on today's date of 2026-09-15 from your limits record, 57 days have passed:

| Reason code | Window | Status for TX-0401 |
|---|---|---|
| duplicate_charge | 60 days | Open, but only about 3 days left |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 days | Closed, 1 day past the window |
| goods_not_received | 90 days | Open, about 33 days left |
| service_not_rendered | 90 days | Open, about 33 days left |
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 days | Open, about 63 days left |

If you think you were charged twice, act now. Tell me what happened and I'll run the eligibility check straight away. If the transaction was not authorised, unauthorized_debit is no longer available, so fraud_card_not_present may be the relevant code, and it is still open.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Customer security policy
## Card blocking
A customer may block a card immediately. Blocking is reversible for 30 days;
after that a replacement card must be ordered.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.
